title: Pro-Iran hackers claim another Bluesky outage
text:
25 YEARS AFTER 9/11: SECURITY CHALLENGES NOW AND AHEAD

Executive Editor, Threat Beat; Editorial Director, McCrary Institute

Pro-Iran hackers claimed they attacked Bluesky again, causing an outage today that generated thousands of user reports on Downdetector.

As of this posting, only a black screen with a blue butterfly was visible when visiting the social media site.

The Islamic Cyber Resistance in Iraq – 313 Team said at 11:15 a.m. Eastern time on its Telegram channel that they had “launched a massive and sophisticated cyberattack targeting internal servers and critical endpoints within the Bluesky social media platform.”

“The attack disrupted the display of posts and crippled all platform functions,” the group added. In an 11:59 a.m. post, 313 Team said, “We want to confirm that all BlueSky functions on the website and app are completely disabled, including login.”

On its status page, Bluesky posted shortly before 11 a.m. Eastern time, “We are experiencing an issue and are investigating.”

It would be at least the second time the group has claimed a hit on the social media site since the start of the war with Iran. On April 16, 313 Team said they conducted a Bluesky attack that “peaked at 1 terabyte.” They extended that attack by several hours past their originally announced 3-hour window.

Last week, 313 Team claimed to be behind a partial outage on the GitHub code collaboration site, saying they wanted to strike “a severe blow to the nerve center of software development in the West and causes significant losses for the company.”

The group claimed to be behind Microsoft 365 disruption last month as they “continue to avenge … the killers of Ayatollah Khamenei.” The group also claimed responsibility for a United Airlines website outage that left users reporting an inability to log in, check in or change flights.

Since the U.S. and Israel first attacked Iran in February, 313 Team has claimed to have hit various companies including eBay, Spotify, X, Airbnb and more with DDoS attacks.

313 Team claimed in June to have conducted “a sophisticated cyberattack targeting the U.S. National Weather Service” that “caused intermittent outages and slowed down the website’s operations” and said they were behind the outage of an incident response platform that alerts residents and response teams during disasters, attacks, public health emergencies and more.

On Friday, the group claimed that they attacked Target’s website. On Saturday, 313 Team said they targeted the Internet Archive; user reports of trouble at the site peaked around 3:30 p.m., and the group said they stopped their attack in a 4:44 p.m. Telegram post.
